explain.say: A hydro turbine is matched to how far the water falls, called the head. A Pelton wheel suits mountains: water falls hundreds of metres down a pipe and shoots out as fast jets that slam into cup-shaped buckets around a wheel.

explain.say: A Kaplan turbine suits rivers and tidal barrages, where the water falls only a few metres but there is a lot of it. The water flows through blades like a ship's propeller, and the blades can tilt to match the flow.

explain.say: Each litre of water gives energy in proportion to how far it falls. So low heads need huge flows and Kaplan turbines, medium heads use Francis turbines, and high heads use Pelton wheels.

Engineers choose whichever turbine turns the most of the water's energy into spinning at that site. Large hydro turbines can be over 90 percent efficient, among the most efficient machines ever built.

faq.a: A Pelton wheel is a wheel with double cup-shaped buckets around its rim. High-speed jets of water hit the buckets and are turned almost right round, giving nearly all their energy to the wheel. Lester Pelton developed it in the 1870s.
asks: How does a Pelton wheel work?

faq.a: A Kaplan turbine looks like a ship's propeller inside a pipe. Water flows along its axis through blades that can change angle, so it works well even as the river flow changes. Viktor Kaplan invented it in 1913.
asks: How does a Kaplan turbine work?

faq.q: What is the head of a hydro scheme?
faq.a: The head is the height the water falls, from the surface of the reservoir or river down to the turbine. More head means each litre of water carries more energy.
asks: What does head mean in hydro power?

faq.a: A Francis turbine is the most common hydro turbine, used for medium heads from about 10 to several hundred metres. Water spirals in around the edge and flows inwards through curved blades, turning the runner.
asks: Which turbine do big dams use?

faq.q: Why are the Pelton buckets split in two?
faq.a: The ridge in the middle of each bucket splits the jet and sends the water back out to the sides, so it does not splash the next bucket. Turning the water right round takes away almost all its speed, and so its energy.

facts: Large hydro turbines can turn over 90 percent of the water's energy into spinning motion.
Viktor Kaplan invented the Kaplan turbine in 1913.

quiz.say: A mountain lake sits 600 metres above a valley, fed by a small stream. Which turbine fits best?
quiz.show: Best turbine for 600 m of head and a small flow?
quiz.why: Pelton wheels suit very high heads with small flows, where fast jets can hit the buckets.

wrong.1: Kaplan turbines suit low heads with huge flows.
wrong.2: A low-head wheel would waste most of such a big drop.
